change.title: ao-replay/8714-r1
change.description: feat(artifacts): add HTML and Markdown files to GitHub issues
change.author: Aditi Chauhan

findings.title: IPC rejections are shown with Electron's "Error invoking remote method" prefix
findings.body: Both `findArtifactIssues` and `publishIssueArtifact` reject in main with `new Error(stderr.trim() || …)` (`frontend/src/main/github-issue-artifact.ts:16`). Through `ipcRenderer.invoke`, the renderer receives that as `Error invoking remote method 'app:publishIssueArtifact': Error: <message>`. The dialog prints `add.error.message` (line 102) and `issues.error.message` (line 96) as is, so the user sees the internal channel name before the real reason, for example `gh: Resource not accessible by integration (HTTP 403)`. Sibling UIs strip the prefix before display: `frontend/src/renderer/components/ShareArtifactPopover.tsx:127` and `frontend/src/renderer/components/RestartToUpdateDialog.tsx:154`. The `/HTTP 404/` check at line 96 still matches, so only the display is wrong. Strip `/^Error invoking remote method '[^']*': (?:\w*Error: )?/` from both messages. The new tests mock the bridge with plain errors, so none of them covers this.

findings.title: 30 s kill on the publish POST can leave the artifact created while the user sees an error
findings.body: `ghApi` uses `execFile(..., { timeout: 30_000 })` for the POST as well as the reads. The renderer sends the whole file as the body (`ArtifactActionsMenu.tsx:252-258` has no size cap, unlike the 'MAX_ARTIFACT_TEXT_BYTES'-bounded readers). When a large body or a slow network makes gh exceed 30 s, gh is killed after GitHub may already have accepted the request. The callback then rejects with the generic 'GitHub request failed…' message, and the user's natural retry posts a duplicate artifact on the issue. The wait is bounded at 30 s plus one `ensureShellEnv` await, and the failure is visible. Consider a longer timeout for the POST, or wording the timeout error so it says the artifact may already have been added.

findings.title: New IPC handlers trust renderer argument types
findings.body: The sibling `app:listGitHubRepos` handler (line 3897) coerces its argument with `typeof query === "string"`. The new handlers pass `repo`, `query` and `input` straight through. `findArtifactIssues` calls `query.trim()` after `issuePath` has validated only `repo` (`github-issue-artifact.ts:28`), so a non-string query fails with a `TypeError` instead of a validation message. `publishIssueArtifact` relies on the incidental behaviour of `issueArtifactType(input.name)` on a non-string, and it never checks that `input.name` is a plain file name (it is posted as-is in the JSON body). Validate `typeof query === "string"` and `typeof input.name === "string"` in the main-process functions, as `issuePath` already does for `repo`.

findings.title: The search path and its cross-repo filter are untested
findings.body: The only `findArtifactIssues` test covers the numeric lookup of a pull request. The search branch (`github-issue-artifact.ts:33-38`) is untested. That branch builds the `q` string, drops items with `pull_request`, and drops items whose `repository_url` is not the chosen repo. The last filter exists because a user's query can carry `repo:`/`org:` qualifiers that widen the result (see the comment at line 35). Add a test with a mixed result set (other repo, a pull request, a case-different repo name) and assert on the `q` argument.

findings.title: "View on GitHub" fails silently if the returned URL is unusable
findings.body: `publishIssueArtifact` returns `result.trim()` from `--jq .html_url`. If the response has no `html_url`, jq prints `null` or an empty string. `openExternal` then throws 'Unsupported external URL' (`frontend/src/main/external-open.ts:23-25`). The click handler is `void aoBridge.app.openExternal(add.data)`, so the rejection is unhandled and the button does nothing. Either validate in `publishIssueArtifact` that the result is an https URL, or catch the rejection in the click handler.

contracts.action: Menu item 'Add to GitHub issue' reads the artifact and posts it to a GitHub issue via the gh CLI
contracts.equivalent_path: The existing 'Copy as Markdown' action in the same menu (`copy`) reads the file with sessionArtifactFileQueryOptions / fetchSessionArtifactFile.
contracts.before_after: `copy` resolves the URL through `artifactContentUrl` for local sessions and `cloudCpFetch` for cloud sessions, and bounds the read at MAX_ARTIFACT_TEXT_BYTES. `readIssueContent` uses the same URL resolution and fetch functions, then reads the whole body with a fatal UTF-8 decode and no size bound. It is gated on `!iconOnly`, owner, a non-shared cloud session, and an .html/.md extension. A remote-host file is offered the action like Copy is, and takes the same rawUrl path.
contracts.visible_effect: The dialog opens from the menu. Content is read only at confirm time, and the result appears as 'Added to GitHub issue' with a 'View on GitHub' button.
contracts.failure_mode: A missing URL, a non-ok response or a UTF-8 decode failure rejects inside the mutation and shows in the dialog's alert, so it is visible. The decode TypeError text is raw. Nothing is lost for the session.

contracts.action: IPC handlers app:findArtifactIssues and app:publishIssueArtifact spawn `gh api`
contracts.equivalent_path: app:listGitHubRepos and app:getGitHubLogin, which also await ensureShellEnv and run gh with daemonEnv().
contracts.before_after: The siblings swallow errors and return a fallback ([] or ''), and listGitHubRepos coerces its argument types. The new handlers let errors propagate to the renderer, which is right for a write. They add no argument-type coercion, and no sender check, which the siblings do not have either.
contracts.visible_effect: Search results and the published URL reach the dialog through the useQuery and useMutation results.
contracts.failure_mode: gh missing, signed out, a 403/404 or a timeout rejects with stderr or a generic message. The dialog shows it, with the IPC prefix not stripped (finding). The only wait after ensureShellEnv is bounded by execFile's 30 s kill per call, and each handler makes a single call. No state is left broken.

contracts.action: Issue search and selection in the dialog (debounced useQuery; pasted issue link auto-sets repository)
contracts.equivalent_path: GitHubRepoPicker's own debounce/search effect, which cancels stale results.
contracts.before_after: The query key includes repo and search term, so a stale response cannot overwrite a newer one. The repo or the query changing clears the selection and resets the mutation. `loading` covers the debounce window, so a result list is not shown for an outdated term.
contracts.visible_effect: Result rows, a link chip for a pasted URL, or hint and empty states. Confirm stays disabled until `selected` exists.
contracts.failure_mode: Search errors render in a role=alert row. The dialog does not remount on Back, since it is local state in the menu component.

contracts.action: Whole-operation bound of the gh calls (what bounds the wait)
contracts.equivalent_path: listGitHubRepos uses a 15 s timeout, getGitHubLogin 5 s.
contracts.before_after: Each handler runs one execFile with timeout 30_000, and there is no loop or retry (react-query `retry: false`; mutation `retry: false`). The only unbounded-looking await is `ensureShellEnv()` before it, which the siblings also await, and it caches a promise that is retried once for a failed early probe. The 30 s kill on the POST can leave a server-side success (finding).
contracts.visible_effect: Worst case is about 30 s of the 'Adding…' state with the dialog locked (close is blocked while pending), then an error alert.
contracts.failure_mode: Timeout rejects with the generic message; the dialog unlocks.

summary: Feature is well contained: input validation for the repo path, cross-repo filtering of search results, and a bounded 30 s gh call are all sound. The one defect worth fixing is that IPC rejections render with Electron's raw 'Error invoking remote method …' prefix in the dialog, which sibling UIs strip. Smaller notes: a 30 s kill on the publish POST can leave a created artifact while the user sees an error, the new handlers do not type-check their arguments as listGitHubRepos does, the search/filter path has no test, and 'View on GitHub' can fail silently. I read the files only and ran nothing.
